Welcome to Saint Ronan's
Set in the heart of the magnificent Tongswood estate, Saint Ronan’s is a co-educational day and flexi-boarding school for children aged 2 to 13. With 250 acres of woodland, fields, and adventure, our school offers a truly magical environment in which children can grow, explore, and thrive.
At the centre of it all stands Tongswood House; a grand, rambling Victorian mansion once home to the Gunther family of ‘Oxo’ fame. It’s a place full of character and charm, and we’ve worked hard to preserve its unique spirit.
We are proud to “Mind the Magic” of Saint Ronan’s. While we’ve invested significantly in modernising our facilities, including the new Engineering, Art and Computing suites in the Powerhouse, astro turf and the state-of-the-art Collymore Science Laboratories, we’ve remained true to the school’s ethos: a warm, family feel, and a touch of Hogwartian wonder.
Pre-Prep
Where will the magic begin?
Nursery
Saint Ronan’s Nursery provides children with a gentle introduction to school life whilst establishing solid foundations. The Nursery is housed in the Groom’s Cottage and garden, which has a homely feel for the children as they start their education.
Pre-prep
What a wonderful place our Pre-Prep is. Education here is a journey of discovery and adventure. Because we want each child’s individual journey to be filled with excitement and joy, our teachers work hard to create extraordinary spaces for young children to play and learn in.
Prep School
The Prep School is housed in the main mansion where the former reception rooms and bedrooms of the ‘old house’ have been converted to classrooms or dormitories.
‘This place fizzes with warmth, gusto and authenticity’
The Good Schools Guide
Be part of the Magic
Tours are arranged by the Registrar or the School Office and are usually conducted by the Headmaster and his wife.
Discover
what we’ve been up to…
We were delighted to welcome back Old Ronian and Kent Ladies cricketer Jemima Spence for another fantastic visit.
The Reception children enjoyed their trip to Hastings last week. They had a wonderful under watery adventure at the Aquarium and a walk along the beach, followed by a visit to the Lifeboat station.
It was a real pleasure to welcome Dr Sian Williams and her daughter, Evie, back to Saint Ronan’s this week.
​​Our Prep School pupils were treated to an inspiring start to the day when Head Prefect, Eloise, delivered a captivating TED Talk-style presentation to the whole school.
Going to London to watch Matilda the Musical en masse is always a highlight in Class 3 and this year it did not disappoint.
During Cross-Curricular Week, Year 7 visited the Château de Warsy in France. We had a fantastic time and would like to share some of our experiences and highlights.
Every so often an opportunity arises for us to take part in an event that we know the children will not only learn a great deal from, but they’ll also remember for many years.
The Saint Ronan's cricket dinner was a gorgeous evening that brought together 80 parents, Old Ronians, and friends of the school for a night of laughter, generosity, and celebration of cricket. Held in the Great Space, the event summed up the community spirit that encompasses our school.
80 brave pupils from Upper and Remove took part in the Sleep Out to raise funds and awareness for Centrepoint, a charity dedicated to ending youth homelessness. Armed with sleeping bags and cardboard boxes, the children spent the night outdoors to get a small taste of the discomfort many young people face every night.
As Nelson looked down benevolently from his column on the band of brothers (and glamorous sisters) who had convened, not to knock the French from their perch but to celebrate their alma mater on a balmy night in central London, a hugely convivial evening unfolded.

Head Prefect Presentation
Each term, our Head Prefect is given the opportunity to share a subject they are passionate about with pupils and staff and this term Eloise chose to explore some of the greatest sporting personalities in history. Speaking with confidence and enthusiasm, she reflected on the determination, resilience and mindset that have helped these athletes achieve extraordinary success.
Eloise rounded off her presentation with a fun quiz and prizes, which proved a huge hit with pupils and staff alike.
Her confidence, warmth and ability to engage pupils of all ages shone throughout the talk. It was wonderful to see our younger children so inspired by her enthusiasm and leadership and to watch them realise that one day, they too could be standing at the front of the room, sharing their own passions and ideas.
Congratulations to Eloise on her thoughtful, engaging and memorable presentation.

2025 Year 7 French Trip
Monday: Our journey began with a visit to our pen-pals' school in Le Touquet. We played various games, which was great fun!
Tuesday: Our first full day at the pod village started with a visit to a traditional French goat farm. We met Dumbledore, a goat with a magnificent beard, and fed him and his friends. We also milked a goat and learned how the milk is turned into cheese. Towards the end, we saw some ferrets and rabbits - even the rabbits in France eat baguettes! Finally, we tasted some fresh goat cheese, which was delicious.
Wednesday: We travelled to Paris and took a ride on the famous Bateaux Mouche down the River Seine. We saw many French landmarks, including the Eiffel Tower, Notre-Dame and the Louvre. Afterwards, we drove around the Arc de Triomphe. Finally, we climbed 166 steps in 37-degree heat to the beautiful Basilique du Sacré-Coeur de Montmartre, where we enjoyed a stunning view of the Parisian skyline.
Thursday: We visited a typical French market where we bought baguettes and souvenirs. In the afternoon, we explored the underground city of Naours and saw graffiti dating back to WWI. The tunnels, 30 meters below the surface, were intricate and winding. We had to wear hard hats for protection, making us look like we were on a construction site.
Friday: We were fortunate to visit a French bakery, where a rather intimidating 'boulanger' taught us how to make croissants. Afterwards, we bought some lovely cakes and more baguettes from their shop, depriving the locals of their daily essentials.
Some of the highlights included the workers at the château (Giuseppe and Armand), the afternoon activities and the talent show, which was won by the Toe Walkers! We also enjoyed playing the murder mystery game throughout the trip.
By Rowan M, Max Z, and Will G

pageCache.pageTitle: Upper & Remove Sleep Out for Centrepoint
pageCache.text:
Upper & Remove Sleep Out for Centrepoint
The pupils started with a range of team-building challenges, brilliantly set up by Mr Maw, Mr Marley, Mr Taylor-Young, Mr Best de Wynter and Mr Gairdner. Their time and energy helped make the evening not only meaningful but memorable and engaging. A huge thank you is owed to them all.
Our intrepid fundraisers then queued up with mugs and bowls at the makeshift soup kitchen to collect a simple supper before heading off to their respective areas to make their sleeping arrangements.
The girls settled under the sports hall veranda, offering some protection from the elements, whist the boys began by the Terrace Wall. However, at around 3am, torrential rain forced a reluctant but necessary move into the Great Space to complete the night.
Thanks to the incredible spirit of the pupils, the generosity of supporters, and the dedication of staff, the event raised over £4,000 for Centrepoint. It was a powerful reminder of the importance of empathy, community, and action.

Drama
at Saint Ronan's
At Saint Ronan’s, drama is at the heart of inspiring creativity and confidence in the children.
Our vibrant programme encourages every child to express themselves, take risks and discover the joy of performance in a fun, supportive environment.
From the very first lesson, pupils learn to use their voice, imagination and movement to bring stories to life - developing communication skills and self-belief that extend far beyond the stage.
Weekly drama lessons are offered to Years 3 to 5. Pupils who wish to take their passion further can join LAMDA with Chrissie Yates, Director of Invicta Youth Theatre. Through solo and group work, children prepare for graded exams and perform their pieces at the Autumn Term Friday Gathering showcase - a highlight of the year!
Every term offers something different for pupils and their families to look forward to:
Beyond the stage, we celebrate public-speaking and performance through the Poetry by Heart competition, where pupils recite poetry from memory, with finalists performing at The Globe Theatre, London.
Children also play an active role in chapel services and assemblies, sharing readings, prayers and poems with confidence and pride.
At Saint Ronan’s, we aim to ignite a lifelong love of theatre and the arts, helping every child find their voice - and the confidence to use it.

Music
at Saint Ronan's
Music is woven into life at Saint Ronan’s. From the joy of early music-making to the thrill of ensemble performances, every pupil is encouraged to explore, perform and discover the power of music.
Class Music
Our aim is simple: to inspire children to perform, while giving them the knowledge and confidence to understand and enjoy music in all its forms.In the Early Years, lessons focus on music and movement, building a strong foundation in rhythm and pitch.
As pupils progress through Years 5–8, they journey chronologically through the great periods of Western classical music, developing an understanding that allows them to appreciate and perform world, folk, jazz and pop music with real context and curiosity.
Instrumental Tuition
Every child begins their instrumental journey with a term of free violin tuition in Year 3, before moving on to the recorder in Year 4. From there, pupils are encouraged to explore brass, woodwind, strings or the saxophone. They learn keyboard skills in Year 5 to support the class band sessions in Year 6.
Individual lessons are also available in piano, guitar, drums, singing and music theory, giving every child the chance to find their musical voice.
Our Peripatetic Teachers
Saint Ronan’s is home to sixteen exceptional peripatetic music teachers; each a professional musician passionate about sharing their craft. They teach the full range of orchestral instruments, as well as voice, piano, percussion and theory. Many pupils work towards ABRSM exams, while others simply play for the love of it. Because every child’s musical journey is personal, their progress is celebrated in many ways.
Performance opportunities
Performance is central to music at Saint Ronan’s. Throughout the year, pupils take part in a rich programme of concerts and events:
These experiences help our young performers grow in poise, confidence and pride.
Ensembles
Collaboration is at the heart of music-making. From String Theory for Year 3s to our Senior Strings, Wind Band and full School Orchestra, pupils experience the joy of performing together. Our ensembles have played works by Sibelius, Beethoven, Strauss and John Williams, performing in front of packed audiences at the four major concerts each year.
Choirs
Singing is the heartbeat of Saint Ronan’s. Every child in Years 3 & 4 sings in a choir, and the joy of group singing continues through Years 5-8.
Our 45-strong Chamber Choir, led by professional opera singer Frances Bourne, performs at major school events, while the Chapel Choir leads services and sings Evensong both at school and in local churches.
In May 2025, the Chapel Choir recorded A Season to Sing with St Dunstan’s, Mayfield for Signum Records - a proud moment for all involved.
Scholarships and Success
Saint Ronan’s musicians regularly achieve outstanding success. Pupils who reach ABRSM Grade 5 become Music Scholars, receiving free lessons on their chosen instrument.
Over the past four years, our pupils have earned 32 scholarship awards to leading senior schools, including King’s Canterbury, Hurst, Sutton Valence, Tonbridge, Mayfield, Sevenoaks and Benenden.
Above all, we hope that every Ronian leaves the school with a lifelong love of music and performance, and the confidence to keep making it, wherever their journey takes them.

Chapel
at Saint Ronan's
We love our Chapel and take joy in our services, which are held on a Monday morning for Nursery & Pre Prep and a Tuesday morning for the Prep School. We also meet for two or three Friday Evensongs per year, taken by a local vicar.
The Chapel is one of the only vestiges left of the original building in Worthing. It was dismantled there and reassembled – brick by brick – where it stands today. In 2014, Old Ronians paid for the Chapel Corridor to be redesigned and created a memorial garden to Old Ronians who were killed in the two World Wars.
Music plays a prominent part in the life of the Chapel. We love to sing together, have an exceptional Chapel Choir and enjoy the beauty of hearing the children singing solos or playing instrumental pieces. The children in Year 8 all read in Chapel at least once during the academic year.
Chapel is, and will remain, a much-loved and a very special place in the school. It embodies all that is best about our pastoral approach and what really matters.

Charitable
Structure
Upon his death in 1957, the school’s third Headmaster, W.B. Harris, made two generous bequests. The business, Saint Ronan’s School, was left to Sir Richard Vassar-Smith. Tongswood Estate, which he had purchased in 1945 to house the school, was left in trust for Saint Ronan’s School’s continued use and benefit. This trust is called the W.B. Harris Will Trust and is independent of the school itself, with its own board of trustees.
Sir Richard Vassar-Smith took over the school and two generations of Vassar-Smiths made Saint Ronan’s their home and life. Sir John Vassar-Smith retired in 1997. At this point, he converted the School from a proprietorial business to an educational trust.
There are thus two separate charitable trusts. The first is the Harris Will Trust, who are the freeholders of the estate. The second is Saint Ronan’s School which, as life tenant of the W.B. Harris Will Trust, has the right to occupy the estate and receive all its income in perpetuity. The list of the school’s trustees is published online.
The two charitable trusts are separate entities but the School and the Harris Will Trust, as landlord and tenant, meet regularly and work closely together.
In 2009 a third charity, The Saint Ronan’s Appeal Fund, was set up by the Harris Will Trust. Its function is to assist the Harris Will Trust in financing the development of the estate. The trustees of the Harris Will Trust are the trustees of the Appeal Fund. The school has been appointed as agent to the Saint Ronan’s Appeal Fund, allowing it to manage the raising of funds from the school community.
The recent Campaign for the Sports Hall shows how these three Trusts, although separate, work together. The school, in its role as agent to the Saint Ronan’s Appeal Fund, managed the raising of funds from its community members. The funds raised were collected by the Appeal Fund to part finance the construction of the Sports Hall by the Harris Will Trust, who will be the owners of the new building.

pageCache.pageTitle: Kent Ladies Cricketer & OR - Jemima Spence
pageCache.text:
Kent Ladies Cricketer & OR - Jemima Spence
Jemima joined us for games, putting our Midway and Upper girls through their paces in the nets, offering expert tips and encouragement that really inspired everyone to step up their game. The fun continued with our juniors in years 3 and 4, who treated Jemima to a lively game of Kwik cricket. There was plenty of excitement and some wonderful cricket on display as Jemima supported and cheered them on throughout. It’s lovely to have Jemima back again this year, and we are so grateful to her for taking time out of her busy schedule to spend the day with us. Her positivity and passion for cricket made the experience truly special for all involved. We look forward to cheering Jemima on this summer (keep an eye out for her in The Hundred, playing for Birmingham Phoenix!). She’ll be in action at Lord’s against London Spirit on 9th August, so be sure to follow and show your support!
Latest News

Life in the
Nursery
Our Nursery is a place where little fingers can feel mud, sand, flour and paint. It's where eyes light up at the sight of smiles, friends, birds and trees and where feet can wander across grass and soil, discovering the world one step at a time. Here arms are always ready for hugs, in a space where children feel safe, seen and ready to grow.
Sessions
Every child is different so we believe that you should be able to choose the right number of sessions for your child. However, we do ask that they do a minimum of 2 full days or 3 half days, as this helps them settle the best.

Whatever you choose, the children will be served a hot lunch at midday.

Learning Outside
Learning outside is fun when you have so many different environments to explore. Learning and having fun in our Forest & Farm Schools is a weekly highlight for the Nursery children. The children have a beautiful garden where they can take their learning outside. They can cook up amazing recipes in the sand pit and young engineers can work safely in the outdoor construction area, as well as tending to their strawberries and other tasty crops in the vegetable garden.
Forest School
Further afield is the Forest, which we visit twice a week, come rain or shine. We light fires in the winter and pond-dip in the summer. On very cold days, we toast marshmallows and listen to stories in the Hobbit House. The extensive grounds have beautiful places to explore, such as visiting the bees in the Salt Mines or the wildlife in the wild flower meadow. In the summer we practice our Sports Day races on our athletics pitch and swim in the heated pool.
The Hobbit House
The Hobbit House: it's often said that there's no such thing as bad weather, only bad clothing! However sometimes it's nice to toast marshmallows and keep warm when it is cold outside. The Hobbit House offers shelter and a fire pit just outside our Forest School.
Paradise Farm
Paradise Farm: the School farm, known as Paradise Farm, is an important part of our focus on Learning Outside. We visit the Farm throughout the year, where we meet the pigs and their piglets and collect eggs from the hens, who love a cuddle from the children.
The Orchard & Sophie's Garden
We visit the Orchard & Sophie's Garden throughout the year, whether we are collecting plums and apples to make crumble or going for a learning walk. Sophie's garden provides space for mindfulness and yoga.
Transition from Nursery to Reception at Saint Ronan’s School
In the Nursery, we pride ourselves on ensuring that the children have a comfortable and reassuring transition to our Reception classes. Our special Nursery is located right at the heart of the school, so our young children naturally become part of the wider school community from the beginning of their Saint Ronan’s journey. This allows them to grow familiar with the school environment, the routines and the wonderful teachers, long before they make the move into Reception. Throughout the year, our Nursery children participate in a wide range of Whole School activities. They practise for, and join in with, the Brodie Shield (cross-country), the Founder’s Day concert, assemblies and themed celebrations, such as World Book Day. These exciting opportunities help the Nursery children feel proud, confident and connected to the School.
The Nursery’s close relationship with Reception makes day to day transitions wonderfully natural. Nursery enjoys lunch with Reception in Pudding Lane (the dining room) and we share play times in the Reception garden. The Reception Teachers regularly visit the Nursery to assist with duties so the children become comfortable and familiar with the staff who will soon be teaching them. As summer approaches, we begin to gently increase transition experiences and opportunities. Nursery children visit the Reception classrooms for relaxed story time sessions, helping them get used to the setting. We enjoy a shared Sports Day and Picnic with Reception, building relationships and kindling eager anticipation of the year ahead. Finally, our 'Move‑Up Afternoon' gives Nursery children the chance to spend a full session in their new class, helping them step forwards into Reception with confidence, knowledge and enthusiasm.
To sum up, our immersive, inclusive approach ensures that moving from Nursery to Reception is not a big leap - it's just a natural, happy next step.

Life in the
Pre-Prep
What a wonderful place our Pre-Prep is. Education here is a journey of discovery and adventure. Because we want each child’s individual journey to be filled with excitement and joy, our teachers work hard to create extraordinary spaces for young children to play and learn in.
At Saint Ronan’s, a stimulating and varied curriculum is used to guide our children in exploring and gaining an understanding of the world around them. Each child is encouraged to think for him or herself and to ask the question ‘why’. Characteristics such as imagination, awareness, perseverance, cooperation, curiosity and empathy are encouraged throughout the school.
The Saint Ronan’s Pre-Prep provides the children with a wonderful opportunity to take risks in a safe environment. Our ambition is to equip our children with the skills to become active thinkers and learners, thereby allowing them to become confident about making a positive difference in our ever-changing world. We do this by giving them the opportunities to discover the outdoors through Forest School, visits to Paradise Farm, romping through our lovely grounds and by providing an enriching and creative indoor curriculum.
A deep care of each child’s wellbeing as an individual lies at the heart of everything we do. We believe that children who are confident and happy are able to be inspired by what they are learning.
It is a place where hobbit houses are built in the woods and where the magic of stories inspires the children to write, read and act out their own compositions. It is also a place where the children’s personal achievements are celebrated, however big or small they are.
